#001

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00001
High Custom + axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A High - detected by both engines
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .menuzord-brand | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a class="menuzord-brand pull-left flip pt-5 pb-5" href="https://jnu.ac.bd/">
    <img src="https://jnu.ac.bd/assets/new/images/logo.png" alt="">
    </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

Custom scanner evidence

Link has no accessible name. Add meaningful link text, aria-label, or image alt text.

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" class="menuzord-brand pull-left flip pt-5 pb-5" href="https://jnu.ac.bd/">
<img alt="" src="https://jnu.ac.bd/assets/new/images/logo.png"/>
</a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

#015

Heading hierarchy may be inconsistent

heading-order  •  UF-00015
Medium Custom + axe Headings WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships Level A High - detected by both engines
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Unexpected heading-level jumps can make the relationship between sections harder to understand.

Location

DOM selector: .mt-15.row > .col-lg-4.pad30.col-md-4:nth-child(1) > .border-de.widget > article > .post-right > .mt-0.post-title | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<h5 class="post-title mt-0 "><a href="https://jnu.ac.bd/faculty/portal/5001" class="font-18 font-weight-600">Faculty of Arts</a></h5>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Heading order invalid

Custom scanner evidence

Heading level jumps from H2 to H5.

axe description

Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct

Recommended change

Review the document outline and use heading levels according to the logical content hierarchy.

Manual review

Required: Yes

A heading-level jump is not automatically a WCAG failure. The full document hierarchy must be reviewed.

#027

Image has an empty alternative

empty_alt  •  UF-00027
Medium Custom Images WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content Level A Contextual/manual review Context-aware recommendation
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Empty alt text is appropriate for decorative images but may hide meaningful content when used on informative images.

Location

DOM selector: nav#menuzord-right > a.menuzord-brand.pull-left > img | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<img alt="" src="https://jnu.ac.bd/assets/new/images/logo.png"/>

Custom scanner evidence

Image has an empty alt attribute.

Recommended change

Keep alt="" if the image is decorative. If the image communicates information or performs a function, replace the empty value with meaningful alternative text.

Context-Aware Recommendation

Visually inspect the image. If it communicates information related to “Home About Chancellor Vice Chancellor Treasurer Syndicate Academic Council Registrar About University Vision & Mission Historical Outline JnU at a Glance Facilities Halls Medica...”, replace alt="" with a concise description of what the image actually communicates. If it is purely decorative, keep alt="".

Why this suggestion was made: The surrounding parent text identifies the content context, but textual context alone cannot determine what the image visually contains.

Evidence: parent text Context confidence: low Language: en Decision: EMPTY_ALT_CONTEXT_AVAILABLE

Recommended action: verify decorative or informative

Visual review required

The surrounding text provides contextual evidence, but the image itself must be inspected before final alternative text is written.

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This recommendation was generated by the proposed deterministic contextual decision engine. Context confidence describes the strength of the extracted contextual evidence, not WCAG conformance certainty.

Suggested code pattern 

<img alt="[Describe image if informative]" src="https://jnu.ac.bd/assets/new/images/logo.png"/>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Automation cannot reliably determine whether the image is decorative or informative.

#128

Generic link wording requires contextual review

generic_link_text  •  UF-00128
Medium Custom Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) Level A Contextual/manual review Context-aware recommendation
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Text such as 'Read More', 'More', or 'Click Here' may not clearly identify the link destination when encountered outside its visual context.

Location

DOM selector: div.section-content:nth-of-type(2) > div.row > div.col-md-4.col-sm-4:nth-of-type(7) > div.widget > article.post.border-de > div.post-right > p.pt-5.font-weight-600 > a.btn.btn-theme-colored | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a class="btn btn-theme-colored btn-circled btn-xs font-white font-13" href="https://jnuits.org.bd/">Read More <i class="fa fa-arrow-circle-right"></i></a>

Custom scanner evidence

Link text is generic and does not clearly identify the destination.

Recommended change

Prefer descriptive link text that communicates the destination or purpose. If generic wording is retained, verify that programmatically determined context makes the purpose clear.

Context-Aware Recommendation

Read more: Jagannath University IT Society

Why this suggestion was made: The nearby nearby heading provides a specific description of the destination, so it can be used to make the generic link purpose clearer.

Evidence: nearby heading Context confidence: high Language: en Decision: LINK_CONTEXT_AVAILABLE

Recommended action: replace or expand accessible link name

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This recommendation was generated by the proposed deterministic contextual decision engine. Context confidence describes the strength of the extracted contextual evidence, not WCAG conformance certainty.

Context-Aware Suggested HTML 

<a aria-label="Read more: Jagannath University IT Society" class="btn btn-theme-colored btn-circled btn-xs font-white font-13" href="https://jnuits.org.bd/">Read More <i class="fa fa-arrow-circle-right"></i></a>

Suggested code pattern 

<a class="btn btn-theme-colored btn-circled btn-xs font-white font-13" href="https://jnuits.org.bd/">Describe the link destination</a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Generic wording alone does not prove a WCAG failure; the programmatic context must be evaluated.
